transcript: I hate the word AI called artificial intelligence. I call it Alibaba intelligence. Yeah. And now Jack Ma is onto proving it. I cloned Jack Ma into an AI and asked three toughest questions as a founder, and what came as answers will leave you shocked. Building as a solo founder is tough. Every decision is on you. The pressure, uncertainty, and that 2 AM loneliness. No co-founder, no mentor to call. It made me think of Jack Ma, someone who failed many times building Alibaba, and almost gave up more than once. So I wondered, what if I had a Jack Ma style mentor I could talk to anytime? Using Accio Work, an AI tool from Jack Ma's company, I built a skill that thinks and responds like him. Then I asked him three questions I've never said out loud to anyone. First: Safe or risky—how do I choose? He said, "Safe is the most dangerous word for entrepreneurs. Most people die tomorrow night because they chose the safe path." That line really hit me. I used to overthink safe versus risky. Now I realize safe often means doing what everyone else is doing, and it can trap you for years. Second: What do founders obsess over that actually matters way less than they think? He said, "Fundraising and valuation. Money is just gas, not the destination." This really resonated. We focus too much on investor numbers and forget real user pain. Third: Biggest early mistake at Alibaba? He said, "Hiring impressive people too early. Early teams must be willing to learn, fail, and grind." That hit home. Early on, you need people ready to suffer and believe in the mission, not just shiny resumes. This isn't motivational fluff. It pushes back, challenges you, but feels real. Like an old-school mentor who's been through the fire sitting across from you at 2 AM. If you are also grinding solo and want something like this in your pocket, comment "JackMa" and I'll send you the skill package. I share more skills like this daily in my WhatsApp community.
